note: Main missions. The name is curated Chinese; the description is English by default so a new player always knows what to do. Tapping ? reveals the pinyin. `done` is either a flag recorded in profile.completed, or a metric counted from progress. `where` is what the minimap draws a line to when the mission is tapped.

quests.en: Say hello to Auntie Lin at the tea stall on the west side of the square.
Learn four everyday words with Xiaomei at the practice corner.
Name ten things around town — look at anything and press {collect}.

quests.pinyin: Dài yí fèn jìniànpǐn huí jiā
quests.en: Buy something from Uncle Chen. Haggling works better when he is in a good mood.
Go home and put something new in your room.
Open the shopping street by learning 25 HSK 1 words. Drilling and naming things both count.

quests.pinyin: Yòng Zhōngwén diǎn yí dào cài
quests.en: Order a dish in Chinese at the restaurant, from a table tablet or a waiter.
Visit the home-goods shop on the west side of the square and buy one thing for your room.
Finish one of today’s errands and collect the reward in your journal.
Buy a ticket at the metro station on the square and ride out to the city.

quests.zh: 记下城里人说的一句话
quests.pinyin: Jì xià chéng lǐ rén shuō de yí jù huà
quests.en: Talk to someone on a Yunhai street and keep what they said in your word bank.
Get a shop permit at Qinghe Bank on the west side of the square. The bank opens after your first practice with Xiaomei.
Bring 8 timber, 6 bricks and 4 bolts of cloth (sold at 家居小铺) to the empty lot on the north side of the square, then start building. Once it stands, it pays 18 coins every morning.
In Yunhai, ask the student on the avenue where 一号书店 is, then walk there and go in.
Take a taxi in Yunhai: tell the driver where you want to go.

quests.pinyin: Zài Hǎifēng miànguǎn chī wǎn miàn
quests.en: Order a bowl at 海风面馆 in Yunhai. The cook may teach you a recipe.

quests.pinyin: Zài jiā zuò fānqié jīdàn miàn
quests.en: Cook the tomato and egg noodles the noodle cook taught you, in your home kitchen.
